question: What is the approximate total length of the Northern Plains (from West to East)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2,400 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plains of India stretch approximately **2,400 km from west to east**, covering a vast area across northern India.
 
• These plains span major Indian states such as Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
 
• The plains are formed by the deposition of sediments carried by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra river systems, making them one of the most fertile regions in the world.
 
• They are classified into three major divisions: the Punjab Plains (western part), the Ganga Plains (central part), and the Brahmaputra Plains (eastern part).
 
• These plains support a dense population due to fertile soil, abundant water resources, and favorable climatic conditions for agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formation of Northern Plains:**

 
 
• These plains were formed as a result of millions of years of sediment deposition by the Himalayan rivers.
 
• The alluvial soil in this region is highly fertile, supporting extensive agricultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plains serve as the heartland of Indian agriculture, producing crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
• The plains are home to several major cities, including Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, and Kolkata.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of the Northern Plains:**
 
 
• The Indus River system forms the western plains, including the Punjab Plains.
 
• The Ganga River system forms the central plains, while the Brahmaputra River system forms the eastern plains.
 
 
 
• **Subdivisions of the Plains:**
 
 
• The Bhabar Belt: Narrow belt of coarse sediments near the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• The Terai Belt: Marshy and swampy region located south of the Bhabar.
 
• The Bangar and Khadar: Older alluvium (Bangar) and newer, fertile alluvium (Khadar) regions.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• The plains are a hub for agriculture, trade, and industries due to their flat terrain and fertile soil.
 
• They are densely populated and contribute significantly to the Indian economy.
